subject: Concurrent access to an app with long computation

messages.author: 1c8861b44e960275
messages.subject: Concurrent access to an app with long computation
parts:
Hi,

I'm writing a shiny application that have rather long computations (like 10 seconds, may be even a minute). I'm using shiny-server to host it. The problem is that by default there is only one R session per app and when computation is happening noone can connect to it. What is the best way to deal with this problem? Shoud I write my own scheduler that, for example, will create a worker per session?

---
Alexey Sergushichev

messages.author: 9711d30301c32133
messages.subject: Re: Concurrent access to an app with long computation
parts:
Hi Alexey,

That is a central problem with R's single-threaded model. There have been a few workarounds proposed on the mailing list previously.

The formal solution to this problem will be Shiny Server Professional, which supports a configurable number of processes per Shiny applications (one process per app, one process per visitor, or anything in between). If you're interested in getting more details, please contact Tareef Kawaf (tar...@rstudio.com) who would be happy to get you some more info on the product.

Best,
Jeff

however. With an admitted bias, I think you'd have much better luck with
Pro.

between them with apache's mod_proxy_balancer. I think this solution
will be enough for me. May be it will help some other people.
